'''Leopoldo Soto Norambuena''' (born October 14, 1964), who publishes as '''Leopoldo Soto''', is a Chilean physicist. He works at the Comisión Chilena de Energía Nuclear, where he founded the Plasma Physics and Nuclear Fusion Laboratory.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=PDI - Resultado de Búsqueda |url=https://investigadores.anid.cl/es/public_search/researcher?id=13586 |access-date=2024-05-06 |website=investigadores.anid.cl}}</ref> His main contributions are in [[experimental physics]] ([[plasma physics]] in particular).

The group that he created and leads works on miniaturizing [[dense plasma focus]]<ref>{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo|title=New Trends and Future Perspectives on Plasma Focus Research|journal=Plasma Physics and Controlled Fusion|date=20 April 2005|volume=47|issue=5A|doi=10.1088/0741-3335/47/5A/027|bibcode=2005PPCF...47A.361S|pages=A361–A381|hdl=10533/176861|hdl-access=free}}</ref> devices which can produce similar physics to that obtained in large devices which are only available in large laboratories around the world.<ref name="speedbull1">{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo |author2=C. Pavez |author3=A. Tarifeño |author4=J. Moreno |author5=F. Veloso|title=Studies on scalability and scaling laws for the plasma focus: similarities and differences in devices from 1MJ to 0.1J|journal=Plasma Sources Science and Technology|date=20 September 2010|volume=19|issue=55001–055017|doi=10.1088/0963-0252/19/5/055017|bibcode=2010PSST...19e5017S |article-number=055017|s2cid=122162772 |url=https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/26f2/1bb9c2ed968150a31071eee958b7c24ebd29.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200209135442/https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/26f2/1bb9c2ed968150a31071eee958b7c24ebd29.pdf|archive-date=9 February 2020}}</ref>

He received the B.S., M.S. and Ph.D. degrees in Physics in 1989, 1990 and 1993, respectively, from the [[Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile]]. His Ph.D. thesis was advised by Hernán Chuaqui, and was the first to be granted by a Chilean University in experimental physics. The results of his thesis were published in the journal [[Physical Review Letters]].<ref>{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo |author2=H. Chuaqui |author3=M. Favre |author4=E. Wyndham|title=A Novel Gas Embedded Compressional Z-pinch Configuration|journal=Physical Review Letters|date=2 May 1994|volume=72|issue=18|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.72.2891|bibcode=1994PhRvL..72.2891S |pages=2891–2894 |pmid=10056011}}</ref>

When he arrived at the Comisión Chilena de Energía Nuclear, he started to work in plasmas driven by small transient electrical discharges and small pulsed power devices: [[z-pinch]], capillary discharges and plasma focus.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo |author2=A. Esaulov |author3=J. Moreno |author4=P. Silva |author5=G. Sylvester|author6=M. Zambra|author7=A. Nazarenko|author8=A. Clausse|title=Transient Electrical Discharge in Small Devices|journal=Physics of Plasmas|date=5 January 2001|volume=8|issue=2572|pages=2572–2578 |doi=10.1063/1.1351829|bibcode=2001PhPl....8.2572S |hdl=11336/136317|hdl-access=free}}</ref> His work has contributed to scaling plasma focuses for a wide range of energies and sizes, keeping the same value of ion density, [[magnetic field]], [[plasma sheath]] velocity, [[Alfvén speed]] and the quantity of energy per particle.<ref name="speedbull1"/> Therefore, fusion reactions are possible to be obtained in ultra-miniaturized devices (driven by generators of 0.1 Joules for example),<ref>{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo Soto |author2=Cristian Pavéz |author3=José Moreno |author4=Luis Altamirano |author5=Luis Huerta|author6=Mario Barbaglia|author7=Alejandro Clausse|author8=Roberto E. Mayer|title=Evidence of nuclear fusion neutrons in an extremely small plasma focus device operating at 0.1 Joules|journal=Physics of Plasmas|date= July 2017|volume=24|issue=8|page=082703 |doi=10.1063/1.4989845|bibcode=2017PhPl...24h2703S |hdl=11336/67569 |hdl-access=free}}</ref> as well as they are obtained in bigger devices (driven by generators of 1 megajoule). However, the stability of the plasma pinch highly depends on the size and energy of the device.<ref name="speedbull1"/>

A rich plasma phenomenology it has been observed in the table-top plasma focus devices developed by Soto's group: filamentary structures,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo|author2=C. Pavez |author3=F. Castillo |author4=F. Veloso |author5=J. Moreno|author6=S. K. H. Auluck|title=Filamentary structures in dense plasma focus: current filaments or vortex filaments|journal=Physics of Plasmas|date=1 July 2014|volume=21|issue=7|doi=10.1063/1.4886135|bibcode=2014PhPl...21g2702S |page=072702}}</ref> toroidal singularities,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Casanova|first=Federico|author2=Ariel Tarifeño-Saldivia |author3=Felipe Veloso |author4=Cristian Pavez |author5=Alejandro Clausse|author6=Leopoldo Soto|title=Toroidal high-density singularities in a small Plasma Focus|journal=Journal of Fusion Energy|date= 6 September 2011|volume=31|issue=3|doi=10.1007/s10894-011-9469-1|bibcode=2012JFuE...31..279C |pages=279–283|s2cid=121105885|hdl=11336/268729|hdl-access=free}}</ref> plasma bursts<ref>{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo|author2=C. Pavez |author3=J. Moreno |author4=M. J. Inestrosa-Izurieta |author5=F. Veloso|author6=G. Gutiérrez |author7=J. Vergara |author8=A. Clausse |author9=H. Bruzzone |author10=F. Castillo |author11=L. F. Delgado-Aparicio |title=Characterization of the axial plasma shock in a table top plasma focus after the pinch and its possible application to testing materials for fusion reactors|journal=Physics of Plasmas|date=5 December 2014|volume=21|issue=12|doi=10.1063/1.4903471|bibcode=2014PhPl...21l2703S |page=122703|hdl=11336/180619|hdl-access=free}}</ref> and plasma jets generations.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Paves|first=Cristian|author2=J. Pedreros |author3=A. Tarifeño Saldivia |author4=L. Soto |title=Observations of plasma jets in a table top plasma focus discharge|journal=Physics of Plasmas|date=24 April 2015|volume=22|issue=4|doi=10.1063/1.4919260|bibcode=2015PhPl...22d0705P |page=040705}}</ref> In addition, possible applications are explored using these kind of small plasma devices: development of portable generator as non-radioactive sources of neutrons and x-rays for field applications,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Soto|first=Leopoldo|author2=P. Silva |author3=J. Moreno |author4=M. Zambra |author5=W. Kies |author6=R. E. Mayer| author7=A. Clausse| author8=L. Altamirano| author9=C. Pavez| author10=L. Huerta|title=Demonstration of neutron production in a table top pinch plasma focus device operated at only tens of joules|journal=Journal of Physics D: Applied Physics| date=1 October 2008|volume=41|issue=202001–205503|doi=10.1088/0022-3727/41/20/205215| bibcode=2008JPhD...41t5215S | article-number=205215|hdl=10533/141980|hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Pavez|first=Cristian|author2=Leopoldo Soto|title=Demonstration of x-ray Emission from an ultraminiature pinch plasma focus discharge operating at 0.1 J. Nanofocus|journal=IEEE Transactions on Plasma Science|date=6 May 2010|volume=38|issue=5|doi=10.1109/TPS.2010.2045110|bibcode=2010ITPS...38.1132P|pages=1132–1135|s2cid=30726899}}</ref> pulsed radiation applied to biological studies, plasma focus as [[neutron source]] for nuclear fusion-fission hybrid reactors,<ref>{{cite journal|last=Clausse|first=Alejandro|author2=Leopoldo Soto |author3=Carlos Friedli |author4=Luis Altamirano |title=Feasibility study of a hybrid subcritical fission system driven by Plasma-Focus fusion neutrons|journal=Annals of Nuclear Energy|date= 26 December 2014|volume=22 |doi=10.1016/j.anucene.2014.12.028 |pages=10–14|hdl=11336/33206|hdl-access=free}}</ref> and the use of plasma focus devices as plasma accelerators for studies of materials under intense fusion-relevant pulses.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Inestrosa-Izurieta|first=Maria José|author2=E. Ramos-Moore |author3=L. Soto |title=Morphological and structural effects on tungsten targets produced by fusion plasma pulses from a table top plasma focus|journal=Nuclear Fusion |date=5 August 2015 |volume=55|issue=93011|article-number=093011|doi=10.1088/0029-5515/55/9/093011|bibcode=2015NucFu..55i3011I}}</ref>

In 1999, he was awarded with a Presidential Chair in Science by the [[president of Chile]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=UMCE Board of DIRECTORS |url=https://www.umce.cl/index.php/universidad/organismos-colegiados/junta-directiva}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Center for research and applications in plasma physics and pulsed power |url=http://www.pppp.cl/contenido/investigador.php?varbajada=1 |access-date=2024-05-06 |website=www.pppp.cl}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> In 2007, he was elected as [[Fellow of the Institute of Physics]], UK.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> He was the president of the Chilean Physical Society for 2 periods, from April 2003 to April 2008, and its secretary general from April 2013 to April 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Científico Leopoldo Soto: "Es importante democratizar el conocimiento, la libertad termina donde empieza la ignorancia" |url=https://www.elmorrocotudo.cl/noticia/sociedad/cientifico-leopoldo-soto-es-importante-democratizar-el-conocimiento-la-libertad-ter |access-date=2024-05-06 |website=El Morrocotudo.cl, Noticias de Arica y Parinacota |language=es}}</ref>
